**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restart the IME after restoring the numeric input type**

When a focused dimension or normalization field switches between pixels and percent, assigning `keyListener` restarts the active IME while the listener is still advertising a text input type, and the subsequent `setRawInputType` does not restart it. The [AOSP `TextView` implementation](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/main/core/java/android/widget/TextView.java) shows this ordering explicitly. Consequently, an already-open keyboard can remain in text/integer mode or lack its decimal key after repeated unit switches even though `field.inputType` reports the expected value; the Robolectric property and editable-filter checks do not exercise that active-IME state. Restart the input connection after setting the raw numeric type, at least when the configured type changes on a focused view.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed in 1a726d7a47013be734cdfc4ceefa13f73d4e0778 with a type-aware NumberKeyListener. Its getInputType returns the final integer/decimal mode before TextView.setKeyListener restarts input; there is no later setRawInputType adjustment. API21 TextView bytecode confirms that ordering. A qualifier: the explicit-string DigitsKeyListener on API21 advertises integer mode, so the initial blanket text-keyboard description was too broad; the decimal restart was still wrong.

The new regression first reproduces the prior assignment/raw-type ordering, recording the incorrect mode at the actual TextView→InputMethodManager.restartInput boundary. It then checks repeated corrected integer/decimal transitions, including an unchanged repeated mode, and EditorInfo. The test records through a custom shadow; it does not claim a physical/real IME result. Existing editable-filter regressions remain. Both 140-tag framework probes retain byte-identical results and all 309 host tests pass after the repair. Updated-head Android CI is pending; fresh review requested separately.
